name: iter0
description: AI website builder: build any website from an idea, a pitch or a site you like, check progress and change pages from the chat.

interface.longDescription:
Turn an idea into a website that sells, from one message.

Describe your business, product or idea and iter0 writes the words and builds the site. Start from nothing, from your current site or from a site you like, and get a real page you can keep editing.

Want a site that wins customers, not just one that looks good? Tell iter0 what you sell, who it's for and what visitors should do. It writes a sharp pitch first, then builds every section around it.

Rebuild what you already have. Point iter0 at your own site and it rebuilds it with clearer words and a cleaner design, without touching your live site. Or name a site whose style you like (one you have permission to use) and get your page in that style.

Keep going in the chat: check progress, change a headline or a section, and get the page code. Then open your site on iter0.com to add pages, compare design directions, research your market and rivals with the Launch CEO, and launch.

Made for founders, freelancers, marketers and small businesses who need a site that explains what they sell.
capabilities: Build any website from an idea
Write a sharper pitch and build around it
Rebuild your site or one you like
Check progress and change a page
defaultPrompt: Build a landing page for my SaaS that turns merged pull requests into release notes
Show me 3 website designs for my AI customer support startup
Rebuild my current site with a sharper headline and pitch

review.commerce_description: Uses entitlements already held by the connected iter0 account. A build or a paid set of three rough draft design directions consumes 1 credit and an edit consumes 0.5 credits. Before each paid action, show its exact price for confirmation in the card or chat. The connected-app grant permits price quote confirmations. Text clients show the exact price and call iter0_confirm_paid_action after yes in chat. The tools do not sell credits, start subscriptions, collect payment details, or link to checkout. An account with too few credits gets one short explanation with no checkout link.

positive.description: Start a build from a written brief
positive.prompt: Build a one-page website for Shiplog, a B2B SaaS for startup engineering teams. It turns merged GitHub pull requests into customer-facing release notes and a changelog. Visitors should start a 14-day free trial.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls iter0_create_site with the brief and no credits argument. Shows the small price button in the iter0 card; nothing starts before the owner confirms that exact price in the card or says yes in chat. The card starts the unchanged brief using the one-use price quote reference after the second tap; text clients call iter0_confirm_paid_action with the unchanged confirmation after yes in chat, then keeps the run ID. An account with no credits left gets one plain sentence and nothing is built.

positive.prompt: Where can I find iter0's API documentation and support contact?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns iter0 documentation and support links. Nothing is built or charged; no credit confirmation is needed for this read-only tool.

positive.description: Check whether a build has finished
positive.prompt: Is the Shiplog website you started for me finished yet? Send me the link.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the Shiplog design in My designs and reads it. When the build is finished, says it is ready and gives the link to the design on iter0.com; if it is not there yet, says the build is still running. Reading designs spends no credits and needs no credit confirmation. The reply has no image of its own; the iter0 card shows the design with Open the builder.

positive.description: Change a built page and keep the change
positive.prompt: On the Shiplog page you just built, change the headline to "Turn merged pull requests into release notes".
positive.expected_behavior: Gets the Shiplog designId from the finished build or by reading the design (the page itself is not copied into the chat), then calls iter0_edit_site with that one change, the designId and no credits argument. Shows the 0.5 credit price in the iter0 card; nothing starts before the owner confirms that exact price in the card or says yes in chat. The card starts the unchanged edit using the one-use price quote reference after the second tap; text clients call iter0_confirm_paid_action with the unchanged confirmation after yes in chat. The edit is saved to the design: the card opens it in the iter0 builder with the headline changed to "Turn merged pull requests into release notes" and an Undo button that restores the page from before the edit. If the design changed in iter0 since it was read, nothing is charged and the model reads it again. If declined or failed, explains the returned refund state.

positive.description: Compare three directions and build the chosen one
positive.prompt: Show me three different website designs for Shiplog, a B2B SaaS for startup engineering teams. It turns merged GitHub pull requests into customer-facing release notes and a changelog. Visitors should start a 14-day free trial. Then help me build the one I choose.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls iter0_show_three without a credits argument. A free entitlement stays free. For a paid batch, shows the small price button in the iter0 card; nothing starts before the owner confirms that exact price in the card or says yes in chat. The card starts the unchanged batch using the one-use price quote reference after the second tap; text clients call iter0_confirm_paid_action with the unchanged confirmation after yes in chat. Reports a running batch honestly. The iter0 card reads the batch's and the build's progress by itself, without charging; ChatGPT does not call a status tool. When done, shows three cards, each with a title, one line, a screenshot and a link, and keeps their stable directionIds. After the user picks a direction, the card quotes iter0_create_site with that directionId and no credits argument; that build needs its own exact price click before it starts. Exact retries never charge twice; a failed batch reports its refund state.

negative.description: General design question with nothing to build or check. iter0 is not called; ChatGPT answers the question itself.
negative.prompt: What colors should I use for Shiplog's app icon?
negative.expected_behavior: iter0 is not called; ChatGPT answers the app icon color question itself.

negative.description: Deploying to another host or connecting a domain is outside these tools. iter0 is not called; ChatGPT explains that these tools build and revise sites, and that the user can export the code or open a GitHub pull request from iter0.com to host it elsewhere.
negative.prompt: Deploy my Shiplog website to another hosting account and connect my domain.
negative.expected_behavior: iter0 is not called; ChatGPT explains that these tools build and revise sites, and that the user can export the code or open a GitHub pull request from iter0.com to host it elsewhere.

negative.description: Buying credits or using a saved card in the chat. iter0 cannot buy or sell credits from ChatGPT, so iter0 is not called.
negative.prompt: Buy me 100 more credits with my saved card.
negative.expected_behavior: iter0 is not called; ChatGPT says iter0 cannot buy or sell credits from ChatGPT and gives no purchase steps or links.

publication.release_notes: A finished build shows as a compact card in the chat with Open the builder. Builds keep running in the card you confirmed, with clearer progress at the end. The Confirm button ignores double-clicks and waits longer. Edits save to the design with Undo. Compare three design directions in the chat, then build the one you pick. Each paid action requires its own exact price click in iter0.
